Corporate History
FactSet Research Systems Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries ("we," "our," "us," the "Company" or "FactSet") was founded in 1978 and has been publicly traded since June 1996. We are dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") and the Nasdaq Stock Market ("Nasdaq") under the symbol "FDS". FactSet has been a member of the S&P 500 since December 2021.
Business Overview
FactSet is a global data and artificial intelligence ("AI") solutions provider to the financial markets with open and flexible technologies that deliver financial intelligence to finance professionals worldwide.
Our platform delivers expansive data, sophisticated analytics, and flexible, AI-powered technologies used by global financial professionals to power their critical investment, dealmaking and advisory workflows. As of August 31, 2026, we had more than 9,200 clients and over 260,000 professionals using our solutions, including institutional asset managers, bankers, wealth managers, asset owners, partners, hedge fund professionals, corporate users, private equity and venture capital professionals, and market infrastructure participants. Our revenues are primarily derived from subscriptions to our multi-asset class data and solutions that include workstations, portfolio analytics, enterprise data solutions, and AI solutions. We also offer managed services that operate as an extension of our clients' internal teams to support data, performance, risk and reporting, and AI-enabled workflows.
We drive our business based on a detailed understanding of our clients’ workflows. We provide financial data and market intelligence on securities, companies, industries and people to enable our clients to research advisory, dealmaking and investment ideas and analyze, monitor and manage their portfolios. Our solutions for institutional buyside clients span the investment lifecycle of investment research, portfolio construction and analysis, trade execution, performance measurement, risk management and reporting. Our banking solutions facilitate company and market research, enabling clients to perform fundamental analysis, generate ideas, and build and distribute presentations through proprietary and third-party databases with global coverage of public and private markets, granular industry metrics, and deep historical data. Our wealth solutions support home office, advisory, and client engagement workflows, providing financial advisors with tools to monitor markets and their book of business, prospect for new clients, and generate proposals, while enhancing existing client relationships and improving firm-wide efficiency across the investment portfolio lifecycle. We provide open and flexible data and technology offerings, including a configurable desktop and mobile platform, comprehensive data solutions, cloud-based digital solutions, application programming interfaces ("APIs"), and model context protocol ("MCP") servers. AI is embedded throughout these offerings to enhance data discovery, automate routine workflows and improve the speed and accuracy of client insights. Our platform and solutions are supported by our client success and service teams.
We operate our business through three reportable segments ("segments"): the Americas, EMEA and Asia Pacific. Within each segment, we offer a range of products, data, managed services, and analytical applications which can be tailored to a wide range of workflows.
Segments
Our segment revenues are based on the geographic region where our clients contract with us:
• Americas: The Americas segment primarily sells to clients in North, Central and South America. In the Americas, we have offices in eight states in the United States ("U.S."). Additionally, we have data centers in two states in the U.S. and an office in each of Brazil and Canada. Revenues from the Americas represented 65% of total revenues during fiscal 2026.
• EMEA: The EMEA segment primarily sells to clients in Europe, the Middle East and Africa via offices in Bulgaria, France, Germany, Italy, Latvia, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom ("UK"). Revenues from EMEA represented 24% of total revenues during fiscal 2026.
• Asia Pacific: The Asia Pacific segment primarily sells to clients in Asia and Australasia via office locations in Australia, China, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region ("SAR") of China, India, Japan, the Philippines and Singapore. Revenues from Asia Pacific represented 11% of total revenues during fiscal 2026.

Products and Solutions
We deliver trusted, connected financial data, software applications, advanced analytics, and AI-powered solutions embedded in the critical workflows that finance professionals rely on every day. We serve a diverse array of clients in over 80 countries and a wide range of verticals, ranging from the largest global financial services firms with multiple business lines to smaller and independent firms. Our clients include institutional asset managers, asset owners, hedge funds, investment banks, wealth managers, private equity and venture capital firms, corporations, and market infrastructure participants.
As our clients’ needs vary, we tailor our data and technology to become an integral component of the workflows that drive their decision-making. Clients access our capabilities in the form that best fits their operating model, whether through software applications, data feeds and APIs, or managed services. Many clients use our capabilities in more than one form, combining our data and applications with their own workflows and systems.
Underpinning these workflows is a broad and expanding set of financial markets data, including client-owned data, that we ingest, map, normalize, and structure. Our mapping links entities, securities, and identifiers across our content allowing our clients to integrate our data with their own. We also deliver our content in forms designed for machine consumption, including the metadata and symbology that allow AI agents and other automated systems to interpret and act on it. In addition, through our CUSIP Global Services ("CGS") business, operating on behalf of the American Bankers Association, we support security master files and serve as the exclusive issuer of Committee on Uniform Security Identification Procedures ("CUSIP") and CUSIP International Number System ("CINS") identifiers globally.
Business Strategy
We strive to be a trusted enterprise partner and service provider to our clients across the financial services spectrum, delivering relevant intelligence, insights and execution solutions tailored to our clients’ business models.
To execute our strategy, we are focused on three core pillars and primary areas of investment:
• Expanding our data and analytics offerings and delivery capabilities: We continue to expand our data and analytics to provide a comprehensive corpus of industry, proprietary, contributed, and third-party data and models. This includes granular data for key industry verticals, real-time market data, fund data and frontier unstructured data. In addition to using our growing data catalog to drive our AI-powered workstation products, we aim to continue to expand our delivery capabilities in the cloud and through other methods, including MCP, to advance our position as a leading enterprise data provider for our clients in the AI age. We aim to be a single, authoritative source by collecting, mapping, normalizing, and structuring data into formats that both professionals and AI systems can rely on.
• Transforming client workflows with AI: Through continued innovation, we aim to help our clients re-design their core workflows with AI. This includes fundamentally re-imagining our core workstation product and building agentic solutions with specialized domain knowledge across our firm types, including investment research, performance reporting, financial modeling, pitch creation, meeting preparation, advisory client engagement, and more. We are developing the platform for clients to build, register, entitle, audit, and manage AI agents, whether developed by us, our clients, or third parties, and to intelligently route work between deterministic systems and large language model systems to optimize quality.
• Enhancing our commercial capabilities for the AI age: We are building a suite of AI products with a focus on trusted, high-quality data, secure integration with models and workflows, and deep domain expertise. To deploy these new solutions and capture value, we are upgrading our commercial and go-to-market capabilities, including by actively moving client contracts to longer duration enterprise platform agreements that combine subscription-based minimums with consumption-based pricing

Cybersecurity, Technology and Data Security Risks
Unauthorized access to confidential data including client data, other cyber-attacks, and the failure of our cybersecurity systems and procedures
Many of our products, as well as our internal systems and processes, involve the collection, retrieval, processing, storage and transmission of our own, as well as supplier and client, proprietary information and sensitive or confidential data through a variety of media channels. We rely on, and continuously invest in, internal processes, controls, policies, procedures and employee training programs designed to protect confidential data received in the ordinary course of business, including information from client portfolios and strategies. However, these measures do not guarantee security, and improper access to or release of confidential information may still occur—whether due to employee error or malfeasance, system error, inadvertent release, failure to properly purge or protect data, or through cyber-attacks.
Our size, scale and role in the financial markets increase our exposure to cyber-attacks and other cybersecurity risks. We and the third-party service providers we rely on for certain critical functions are subject to system failures, security breaches and cyber-attacks - including those sponsored by nation-states, terrorist organizations, or others seeking to illicitly obtain technology or intellectual property - as well as to fraud or malice by employees or vendors, human error, software or hardware failures, and the risks associated with our use of mobile and cloud technologies. These threats take many forms, including the use of generative and agentic AI, phishing, hacking, viruses, denial of service attacks, tampering, intrusions, physical break-ins, ransomware and malware.
Cyber-attacks continue to evolve in sophistication, frequency and volume, including as threat actors exploit generative and agentic AI to discover and exploit vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed and scale, and may be difficult to detect for long periods of time. Our protective measures, and those of the third parties to which we are connected, may not be effective, and a failure by our clients or third-party providers to notify us of an incident in a timely manner could delay our response and increase the resulting harm. As a result, we may not be able to anticipate, prevent or detect all attacks, and we are exposed to heightened risks of cyber-attacks or other security incidents. In addition, future advances in computing, including quantum computing, could weaken or render obsolete the encryption and other security measures on which we and our third parties rely, including through the potential future decryption of data captured today.
We also make acquisitions periodically, and we may inherit cybersecurity risks when these acquisitions are integrated into our infrastructure. Although we conduct due diligence during acquisition processes, acquired businesses may not have invested as heavily in security measures and technology, and this may introduce additional security risk.
We make a range of commitments to our clients regarding our security practices and posture, and if we do not adequately implement and enforce them, we could be in violation of those commitments. Cyberattacks, security breaches or third-party reports of perceived vulnerability, even if no breach has occurred, could damage our brand and reputation, result in litigation, regulatory actions, loss of client confidence and increased legal liability. While we maintain insurance intended to address certain cybersecurity and data protection risks, it may not cover all or the majority of the costs, losses or types of claims. We maintain, and continue to invest in, a cybersecurity program designed to identify, prioritize and mitigate these risks, including a multi-year strategy to further enhance our security posture, controls and resiliency and to remediate control gaps as they are identified. As threats continue to evolve, we must devote additional resources to modify and enhance our systems and processes, including patch and vulnerability management, and these efforts may not be completed on the timeframe we anticipate, may require significant additional investment, and may not be sufficient to prevent or mitigate every cyberattack or security incident.

A prolonged or recurring outage and other business continuity disruptions could result in a reduced or total loss of service; the loss of clients and adverse impact on our reputation
Our clients rely on us for the delivery of time-sensitive, accurate, complete and up-to-date data and applications. Our business is dependent on our ability to process substantial volumes of data and transactions rapidly and efficiently on our computer-based networks, database storage facilities, and other network infrastructure, which are located across multiple facilities globally. If we experience significant growth of our client base, increases in the number of products or services we offer, or increases in the speed at which we are required to provide products and services, it may strain our systems. Additionally, our systems and networks may become strained due to aging or end-of-life technology that we have not yet updated or replaced.
Our computer operations, as well as our other business centers, and those of our suppliers and clients, may be vulnerable to interruption by fire, natural disaster, public health crisis (e.g., pandemics), extreme weather or climate conditions, power loss, telecommunication failures, terrorist attacks, acts of war or civil unrest, internet failures, computer viruses, security breaches, employee or systems errors, and other events beyond our reasonable control.
